parameters.content:
## Job Scout: daily scan

Every morning this path scans the Ashby boards listed in **Job Scout config**, saves one lead per posting in the `leads` Data Table, scores the leads that pass the hard filters, and sends the best ones to Telegram.

**Setup**
1. Create a bot with @BotFather and pick its credential on **Send header** and **Send lead message**.
2. Add a Bearer Auth credential with your TypeSafe API key on **Ask Jev**, and an Anthropic credential on **Write fit line**.
3. Fill in **Job Scout config** (see the note below it), including your **profileSummary**.
4. Publish the workflow.

The `leads` table is created on the first run if it doesn't exist. Job Scout never applies for jobs or contacts anyone.

## Job Scout config

Edit these fields in the **Job Scout config** node:

- **ashbyBoards**: Ashby board names to scan, as a list. The board name is the part after `jobs.ashbyhq.com/` in a company's job board link. Default: `n8n`, `posthog`, `ramp`.
- **telegramChatId**: the chat the daily ping goes to. Tap Start in your bot, open `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getUpdates` once, and copy `message.chat.id`.
- **dailyCap**: the most leads one daily ping sends. Leads over the cap stay New and go out on a later day. Default 10.
- **tablePrefix**: put in front of every Data Table name, so `jobscout_` gives `jobscout_leads`. n8n looks tables up by a "name contains" match, so no other table name may contain the full name (for example, don't use an empty prefix if `jobscout_leads` exists). The tests use `jobscout_test_`.
- **roleFamilies**: the kinds of roles you want, each with a `name`, a `description` and the `titleKeywords` that mark it. Jev picks a lead's family from these (or none of them), and every family scores the same. They don't filter anything. Default: DevEx/Product PM, FDE/Solutions, Product/Frontend Engineering, and DevRel/DevEx.
- **excludedTitles**: a posting whose title contains one of these words or phrases is filtered out. Case doesn't matter and only whole words match, so `Finance` doesn't match "Fintech" and `HR` doesn't match "HRIS". Only the title is checked, never the department: developer relations roles often sit in Marketing. Default: non-engineering operations titles (Accountant, Finance, Legal, Counsel, Paralegal, HR, People Ops, Office Manager, Facilities, Executive Assistant). `Marketing` is deliberately not on the list.
- **excludedTitleOverrides**: a title that contains one of these words is never excluded, so "Software Engineer, Finance Platform" is kept while "Finance Manager" is filtered out. Same whole-word matching. Default: Engineer, Engineering, Developer, Software, SWE, Architect, Programmer, Advocate, DevRel, Product Manager, PM, Platform.
- **locationRules**:
  - `usRemote`: keep postings that offer remote work in the US, including ones where "Remote (US)" is only a secondary location. Default `true`.
  - `usCountryNames`: the names that count as the US.
  - `metros`: areas where you'd also take non-remote work. Each has `cities`, `regions` (if a posting states a state, it must be one of these) and `workplaceTypes` (Ashby's `Remote`, `Hybrid`, `OnSite`). Default: Dallas–Fort Worth with its suburbs, remote, hybrid or on-site. Austin is not in the list, so only remote US roles based there pass.
  - A posting with no location, or one that can't be placed, passes and shows as "Location unclear".
- **payFloor**: the lowest yearly base pay you'd take, in US dollars. A posting is filtered out only when its stated USD base salary range tops out below the floor. Equity, bonus and commission don't count. No stated pay, or pay in another currency, passes; the message shows the posting's pay text or "Pay not listed". Default 180000.

- **profileSummary**: a few short lines about you: target roles, core stack, years of experience, domains, the seniority you want, and location. Jev judges stack and domain fit against it, and Claude writes each lead's fit line from it. Keep it short and factual, and don't paste a resume. Changing it makes Jev judge the unsent leads again on the next scan.
- **weights**: points for each sub-score: `roleFamily`, `stack`, `seniority`, `location`, `domain`, `freshness` and `referral`. They're scaled to add up to 100. Default 25, 20, 15, 15, 10, 10, 5. A weight change re-ranks leads on the next scan without new Jev calls.
- **targetSeniority**: the levels that get full seniority points, from Jev's levels `intern_junior`, `mid`, `senior`, `lead`, `staff_plus`, `manager` and `founding`. A posting that states no level gets half the points, and any other level a fifth. Default `senior`, `lead`, `founding`.
- **minFitScore**: the lowest fit score a lead can be sent with. Default 60.
- **freshnessWindowDays**: how many days after a lead is published (or first seen, if that's earlier) it can still be sent. The freshness sub-score falls from full to zero across the window, and only leads inside it are judged by Jev. Default 30.
- **jevModel**: the TypeSafe Jev model version. It's pinned so scores don't shift when TypeSafe ships a new version; changing it makes Jev judge the unsent leads again. Default `jev-1.13.0`.

**Run time** is set on the **Daily scan** trigger, not here, because a trigger's settings can't read other nodes. Default 8:00 in the instance timezone. If n8n is down at that time, the most recent missed scan runs when it comes back.

## Save leads

A lead is keyed by `ashby:<board>:<job id>`.

- **Save lead** upserts on that key, so a second scan updates the posting fields and `last_seen_at` instead of adding a row.
- **Mark first sighting** gives rows with no status yet `status = new` and `first_seen_at = now`. Rows that already have a status keep their first-seen date.

## Daily ping

- **Pick leads to send** chooses leads with status `new`, `filter_result` `passed`, a fit score of at least **minFitScore**, inside the freshness window and with no `sent_at`, highest fit score first, up to `dailyCap`. Leads over the cap stay New and compete again on later scans. If there are none, nothing is sent.
- **Send header** sends "Job Scout: N new leads today" with sound.
- Each lead goes out as its own silent message with an **Open posting** button, one per second. It shows the pay text (or a salary found in the description, or "Pay not listed"), the location or "Location unclear", the fit score with its points per sub-score, and Claude's fit line.
- **Mark sent** sets `sent_at` and saves the fit line right after each message, so no lead is sent twice.

Both Telegram nodes use HTML parse mode and have the n8n attribution line turned off.

## Hard filters

**Apply hard filters** checks every posting on every scan against the rules in **Job Scout config**, in this order: location, pay floor, excluded titles.

- The first rule a posting breaks is saved in its lead's `filter_result`: `location`, `pay_floor` or `excluded_title`. A posting that breaks none gets `passed`.
- Filtered leads stay in the `leads` table and are never sent.
- Every scan checks again, so a rule you edit also applies to leads saved earlier.
- Unknown pay or location never fails a rule.
- An excluded title word doesn't count when the title also has a word from `excludedTitleOverrides`, such as Engineer or Developer.

Location reads Ashby's workplace type, location, secondary locations and their addresses. It ignores `isRemote`, which Ashby sets on many hybrid postings. `location_basis` says why a lead passed: `us_remote`, `metro` or `unclear`. `pay_min` and `pay_max` hold the stated USD base salary per year, when there is one.

options.system: You write one sentence for a job seeker's Telegram message saying why a job posting fits them. Use only facts written in the posting or in the job seeker's profile summary. Do not invent or assume anything that isn't written there: no years of experience, skills, employers, achievements, team details, pay or locations that aren't stated. Name one or two overlaps, and count something as an overlap only when the posting itself names it and the profile names the same thing; don't match look-alike words. If the fit is weak, say plainly what does match. Write one sentence of at most 30 words, in plain text, with no quotes, emoji or preamble.

parameters.content:
## Scoring

Only leads that passed the filters, are New and unsent, and are inside the freshness window are scored.

- **Build Jev requests** builds one request per lead for TypeSafe's Jev, with every question in it: role family (from the title and duties, never the department), stack fit and domain fit against **profileSummary**, whether the posting names a stack, and the seniority level. For a posting with no structured pay, a regex finds dollar amounts in the description and Jev picks the base salary among them, or none.
- A lead is judged again only when its request changes: a new profile summary, role families, model, or posting text. Weights, **targetSeniority** and **minFitScore** are applied in code, so editing them costs no Jev calls.
- **Ask Jev** uses a Bearer Auth credential with your TypeSafe API key (console.typesafe.ai/keys). It retries failed requests; a lead whose request still fails is saved as unscored, isn't sent, and is judged again on the next scan.
- **Score and select** combines the sub-scores with **weights** into a fit score out of 100, every scan. Location, freshness and referral are computed in code. A salary Jev found in the description that tops out below **payFloor** sets `filter_result` to `pay_floor`.
- **Pick leads to send** takes the eligible leads at or above **minFitScore**, highest fit first, up to **dailyCap**.
- **Write fit line** asks Claude (Anthropic credential) for one sentence on why each picked lead fits, using only the posting and the profile summary. Claude runs only for leads that are sent.

Jev costs about $0.0002 per judged lead. Each lead's sub-scores, fit score, Jev's raw answers and the fit line are saved in the `leads` table.

nodeGroups.name: Fetch boards
nodeGroups.description: Makes sure the leads table exists, fetches each Ashby board in the config, and turns each posting into a lead.

nodeGroups.name: Save leads
nodeGroups.description: Upserts each lead on its key, then marks leads seen for the first time as New.

nodeGroups.name: Score leads
nodeGroups.description: Jev judges New, unsent leads that passed the filters when their input changed; code turns the sub-scores into a fit score every scan.

nodeGroups.name: Build the ping
nodeGroups.description: Picks the highest-fit eligible leads up to the daily cap, has Claude write a fit line for each, and sends the header.

nodeGroups.name: Send each lead
nodeGroups.description: Sends one silent message per lead with an Open posting button and saves sent_at and the fit line, one per second.
